questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: To find a country and university that I could see myself live in/study at. Somewhere not too far away and a place where I had an interest in the culture and history.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was somewhat easy because there was an orientation and they were very helpful but it was also a bit overwhelming with all the information - and the whole process of choosing your subjects felt a bit chaotic. It was also sometimes difficult to find the classroom.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Orientation, a tour around campus and there was the international student office which I didn't use throughout the semester.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was very challenging because I started to look a bit late and almost everything was quickly filled up. I was lucky to get a room in their newest student accommodation short before arrival.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I liked that I had to walk about 20 minutes to campus for the exercise and fresh air. It could be a con if it's very far away and you have to use money for the bus all the time for example. But living off campus is a great way not to be in a "campus bobble" 24/7 I would say.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was a long process for several months and you had to be focused on it so you don't forget any deadlines, but the emails with the instructions were very clear and helpful

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: All kinds of help from students, professors and counselors both academic and personal help.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It was easy to register but I just had a hard time choosing the classes.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not other than try to be well prepared

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was very fine for each subject - some were a bit more challenging to follow just because of the subject matter but it was over all not too low or high.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I had only lectures so it was mostly the professors speaking and that suited me well.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Ancient Greek History, Greek Mythology, Irish Film History, Existentialism (Philosophy), Aspects of Irish Folklore and Old English Language.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Something that they're interested in of course but also something that has some relevance to their major.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: There were no unexpected costs

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Beer was a bit cheaper compared to Denmark. The housing was very expensive because it was very modern and had many facilities.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: They had many different societies/clubs for every kind of interest so that was cool.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Not anything specific just that you should find something you're interested in.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Exploring the city and the rest of the country to get to know the local culture even better. It can also be small things like eating breakfast in town or going to the cinema.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy - the weather was perfect, actually a little bit warmer than in Denmark, the people were super friendly and their pub culture is great.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Not really because it was hard to get to know the locals unless you really put in the effort.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: It was a challenge sometimes to undertand the accent but that's about it. On a funnier note you also kind of have to learn how to drink Guinness when you're in Ireland and that was a bit of a challenge as well.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The pub culture mostly

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Look for housing as soon as possible, perhaps join a club at university, and then just try to experience the culture by going to pubs and explore the city.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: It's not very important to decide before hand which subjects you want to take as you get the opportunity to try them out at the beginning of the semester before making your final decision.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: To try and study at another university, and this one in Cork in particular, which was very old and beautiful. To be able to explore another culture and travel.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Making friends, especially with the locals. I was lucky to know two other Danish girls so we had each other, but socializing in general and have someone you're close with was the greatest challenge.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
